subject: Seller ledger timestamp gap + payout hold — evidence and release plan
messages:
From: Alex Turner <finance@edgescale.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 1 Aug 2029 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Seller ledger timestamp gap causing payout hold — evidence attached

Hi Sean / Karthik,

We're seeing a $45,231.12 hold against our July 31 marketplace payout. Our accounting flagged ~1,200 usage rows that appear to have timestamps outside of the invoice period (some stamped 2029-08-01 UTC) and the marketplace reconciler put those into a pending state. We believe this is a timestamp ingestion gap (likely daylight-savings related) rather than duplicate billing.

I've uploaded two exports to S3 and attached a small sample CSV: edgescale_metering_bucket.csv (sample rows + usage ids). Full exports: s3://edgescale-uploads/2029-07/edgescale_metering_bucket.csv and s3://edgescale-uploads/2029-07/edgescale_full_invoice_export.zip.

Can the team triage and confirm whether these rows can be re-bucketed into the July invoice period? Edgescale needs the funds to cover payroll — requesting expedited review.

Attachments: edgescale_metering_bucket.csv (CSV, 1.1MB)

Thanks,
Alex Turner
Head of Finance, EdgeScale
alex.turner@edgescale.com

- Do the affected usage rows have duplicate usage_id values, or are they unique but stamped outside the invoice window?
- Can you confirm the seller entity / tax id used on the July invoice for the affected rows (we'll need to cross-check entity mapping).

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 3 Aug 2029 14:55:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Seller ledger timestamp gap causing payout hold — technical findings + recommended action

Team — I ran the ingestion traces on the sample file Alex provided and pulled the raw event logs. Summary:

- Root cause: a DST edge case in our AWS Marketplace ingestion lambda for the America/Los_Angeles zone caused some records with event_time close to midnight UTC to be converted to the following UTC day. The conversion path dropped the local tz flag on a subset of records in our July batch; those records therefore landed in the August window during aggregation.
- Impact: ~1,218 usage rows, gross amount $45,231.12, all mapped to EdgeScale seller entity (entity_id ES-881).
- Fix: We'll patch the ingestion path to preserve the original event timezone and re-run the July aggregator for the affected partition. Patch is tracked in SUP-4123.

Recommended immediate actions:
1) Re-aggregate the affected partition and produce a deterministic tie-out CSV (we'll add a reconciliation checksum column).
2) Finance to accept the deterministic tie-out and issue a manual journal to release $45,231.12 to EdgeScale. (Finance owner: Marissa Cole)
3) Post-mortem: update ingestion tests to include TZ edge-cases and schedule a canary run for next batch.

I've attached a snapshot of the SUP ticket and a pointer to the re-aggregation s3 path. Please confirm Finance can proceed with the manual journal and I'll push the re-agg artifacts by EOD Sun.

Attachments: jira_SUP-4123-snapshot.txt
Links: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/SUP-4123, s3://redwood-recon/2029-07/reagg/ES-881/

- Karthik
Lead, Marketplace Ingestion

- Marissa (Finance): please review the tie-out and, assuming parity, execute a manual journal to release $45,231.12 to EdgeScale by Wed 2029-08-07 EOD. Share the journal id once complete.
- Sean: I'll coordinate with Alex to obtain the signed attestation from EdgeScale if Finance needs it for audit.
- Vanessa: track the post-mortem action items (SUP-4123) and ensure TZ edge-case unit tests are added; confirm next release window includes the fix.

Alex / Maya: we'll set a short call tomorrow at 10:30 PDT to walk the tie-out once Karthik uploads the artifacts — please confirm availability.

I'll mark this thread as priority and follow up after the journal posts. Thanks everyone for moving quickly on a payout-sensitive case.
